title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1LC0RB_0LD1LA_0RA1LE_0LA0RA_1LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1LC0RB_0LD1LA_0RA1LE_0LA0RA_1LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean now proves whole rounds, not just sweeps: from a round start A> (10)^4 110 (10)^N 10010 T, for every N in a residue class mod 4 and the short or long tail T, the machine reaches the next round start, with an exact step count (four branches: N → (3N+5)/2, 9N/4 + 24, 11N/4 + 47/2 (with the tail's length), (3N+10)/2). Chaining them from blank tape, Lean's kernel proves that the machine reaches the round with N = 19,199 at exactly step 1,842,640,229 without halting. The tail keeps changing shape (a new one appears at N = 19,199), so the rounds do not yet close into a single map whose orbit decides the question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 51,188 cells have been visited and 26,870 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.065).

claims.title: The counting sweep
claims.text: For all a, b, c and any tape R further right: A> (10)^(a+1) 110 (10)^(b+2) 10010 (110)^(c+1) R (A at the left end of the tape) reaches A> (10)^(a+4) 110 (10)^b 10010 (110)^(c+2) R in 14a + 8b + 83 steps: one sweep moves the counter (a, b, c) to (a+3, b−2, c+1). Also the shift rules the sweep is made of.

claims.title: Four branches of the round map, for all N
claims.text: With RS(N, T) the round start A> (10)^4 110 (10)^N 10010 T (A on the leftmost cell, blank tape left), the short tail Ts = (10)^11 1, the long tail Tl(m) = (10)^m 1 (10)^11 0101 and TD(p) = 1 (10)^p 1 (10)^9 0101101: for all j and m, RS(4j+5, Ts) → RS(6j+10, Tl(3j+6)); RS(4j+2, Tl(m)) → RS(9j+m+27, Ts); RS(4j+4, Ts) → RS(9j+33, Ts); RS(4j+4, Tl(m)) → RS(6j+11, TD(3j+m+5)), each in an exact number of steps. A round is the first sweep (sweep0), the counting sweeps chained by induction (sweeps: k sweeps in k(14a+8x+83) + 29k(k−1) steps) and a conversion found and proved as one symbolic run by bbtools.symtm.

claims.title: Eight conversions
claims.text: The conversion at the end of the counting phase is proved, as a single symbolic run, for every residue of N mod 4 and both the short and the long tail (families A–H); four of them end at a proper round start and are chained above, the other four (N ≡ 3, or N ≡ 1 with the long tail, …) end at a left-end configuration of a different shape.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1,842,640,229 steps
claims.text: From blank tape the machine reaches RS(13, Ts) in 1817 steps and then, by the proved branches A B C A B A B C A D, the round starts N = 22, 84, 213, 322, 909, 1366, 3780, 8529, 12796 and 19199, the last one at exactly step 1,842,640,229: no halt before (the kernel, no native_decide).

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: F on a 1 halts, and F is entered only from A on a 1 (writing 0, moving left), so the machine halts exactly when A reads a 1 with a 1 to its left: 1 A> 1 reaches F on a 1 in one step (the converse direction by reading the table, not formalized).

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In 10<sup>9</sup> steps A reads a 1 92,274,763 times, every time with a 0 to its left.

claims.title: Rounds and the map on N
claims.text: The rounds seen in the run from blank tape, all now covered by the proved branches up to N = 19199 (step 1,842,640,229): N = 7 (tail 1 1 0 1), 13, 22, 84, 213, 322, 909, 1366, 3780, 8529, 12796, 19199. In the old notation (10)^4 110 (10)^N 100 T: (N, short) with N ≡ 0 (mod 4) → 9N/4 + 24; N ≡ 1 → (3N+5)/2 with a long tail; (N, long) with N ≡ 2 → 11N/4 + 47/2 back to the short tail; (N, long) with N ≡ 0 → (3N+10)/2 with the new tail TD.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The proved branches carry the run to N = 19199, but the round from there (N ≡ 3 with the tail TD) ends in a left-end configuration of a new shape, and new tail shapes keep appearing, so the rounds are not yet a closed map. The halting configuration 1 A> 1 never occurs in the proved rounds (they are exact runs), so a halt, if any, would come later. A macro simulation (words 10, 110, 10010) finds the next left-end start at step 4,516,954,072: A> (10)^4 110 (10)^28802 1 110 (10)^30401 110 (10)^5 10010 (110)^2 1, where the run is followed by 1 110 instead of 10010.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LA_0RC1RD_0LD1RE_1LA0RF_0RD0LD_1RD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine runs in rounds that act on a number N like a Collatz map; Lean proves four branches of that map for every N and follows them for 1,842,640,229 steps without a halt. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and explains the rounds.

facts.text: No halt, proved in Lean through 11 proved rounds.
Of the round map, proved for all N.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Pairs and triples
html: Almost the whole tape is made of the pairs 10 and the triples 110. At the start of a round, with the head in A on the leftmost cell, it reads
for example with N = 3780 at step 21,312,041 (the tail can also be a longer word, see below).

sections.heading: Counting down by two
html: During a round the tape is (10)^a 110 (10)^b 10010 (110)^c .... Each sweep runs right into the (10)b part and back, and moves the marker 110 along: a grows by 3, b shrinks by 2, and one more 110 is added on the right. Lean proves this for every a, b, c, with its exact cost 14a + 8b + 83 steps. The sweeps never cross the (110)c part, and the left end gains 5 cells per sweep: the square-root side of the tape.

When b reaches 0 or 1, the (110)c part is converted back into pairs, which gives the next N. Lean proves each such round from start to finish, for every N in a residue class (writing the tail after 10010; the short tail is (10)^11 1, the long one (10)^m 1 (10)^11 0101):

N = 4j+5, short tail:  N' = 6j+10, long tail with m = 3j+6     13 -> 22, 213 -> 322, 909 -> 1366, 8529 -> 12796
N = 4j+2, long tail:   N' = 9j+m+27, short tail                 22 -> 84, 322 -> 909, 1366 -> 3780
N = 4j+4, short tail:  N' = 9j+33, short tail                   84 -> 213, 3780 -> 8529
N = 4j+4, long tail:   N' = 6j+11, new tail                      12796 -> 19199

Each round is three proved pieces: the first sweep, the counting sweeps (chained by induction, k sweeps in k(14a+8x+83) + 29k(k−1) steps), and the conversion, which turns out to be a single symbolic run once the (110)c part is written in pairs (110110)^j: the head crosses every long run by a shift rule. Chained from blank tape (lean/Round.lean), these four branches give the rounds 13, 22, 84, 213, 322, 909, 1366, 3780, 8529, 12796 and 19199, reached at exactly step 1,842,640,229. A Collatz-like map: multiply by about 1.5 to 2.75, the branch chosen by the remainder of N mod 4 and the tail left behind.

sections.heading: A 1 next to A
html: The machine halts when F reads a 1, and F is only entered from A reading a 1 and stepping left. So it halts exactly when A reads a 1 with another 1 just to its left. The proved rounds are exact runs, so no halt happens in the first 1,842,640,229 steps. After that the tail has a new shape, the round from N = 19199 ends in a configuration that is not a round start of the same kind, and the map has not been pinned down in general: like other Collatz-like machines, deciding it would need to know every branch the orbit of N ever takes.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.065).
After 109 steps the tape spans 51,188 cells (34,955 left of the start, 31 right), with a density of 1s of 0.525.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A Collatz-like map with residues mod 4: each round counts a run (10)^N down two cells per sweep, then rebuilds it into a new N of about 1.5 to 2.75 times the size; four branches of the round map are proved in Lean, carrying the run from blank tape to step 1,842,640,229.
